resources.string: Lets DSH read the text on a screen and exactly where it is, which means fewer on-device OCR calls
Keeps the DSH host reachable while the app is in the background
For when what the host reads once (where the workspace lands, the LAN switch) changed
Use smooth rounded rectangles on rounded UI elements
Swipe a pushed page to go back
Let DSH read the screen through the accessibility service
Once on, the model reads the text and the exact position of every control on the screen
Let DSH read the notification shade
Once on, the model can list what is in the shade and dismiss it; turning it on also lets a notification come up as a banner over the lock screen
Scale a screenshot to this many pixels before the model sees it
Shrink a PNG further while it is over %1$d bytes, which is the ceiling this app sets; the route has its own limit in settings.yaml (imageMaxBytes), and a picture over that fails the model request
In KiB, and typing goes up to %2$d; a value over the slider top %1$d needs imageMaxBytes raised in settings.yaml first
%1$d ms between one frame and the next; one capture costs 200-400 ms on its own, so this is what it asks for, not what it gets
%1$d frame(s) each time the camera is asked to look; the agent can name another number for one call, and this is the default it starts from
Capture at up to %1$d pixels; it takes effect the next time the camera opens, and the app reopens it right away when it is already running

Lay the frames out as one picture as well; the agent reads that one first, so a dozen frames cost one look instead of twelve. Each cell is a smaller copy, so it is for seeing what moved, not for reading small text

These are the app\'s half of the video mode camera: how many frames, how far apart, how big, and whether they also come back as one grid. The route has its own budgets in settings.yaml (imagePixelBudget, imageMaxBytes), and a picture over those is re-encoded on the host before the model sees it
Listening for %1$s; a hit or a tap on the ball listens for one sentence
Listening for %1$s, and the resident chain is running too (what video mode asks for: it keeps listening after a sentence)
Allowed to wake, but the service is not running; turn the switch off and on again
Not listening; the switch below starts it
The microphone permission is not granted yet; the Permissions section below has the entry
Model ready: %1$d files, each checked against its sha256
Not downloaded yet, about %1$s in all
%1$d of %2$d files are in place; tap to fetch the rest
Nothing set yet; the default %1$s is what is being watched for (tap to change it)

One word per line, written as word=pinyin with tone numbers, for example 肥鱼肥鱼=fei2 yu2 fei2 yu2. The pinyin becomes the symbols the model knows, and anything missing from its table is refused instead of dropped quietly
Let this app listen for the wake word (a local 3.3M keyword model, 5.3 MB). It is only permission: the microphone starts guarding that word once this is on, and the notification keeps a Stop button

Stops the wake word listener only: the microphone goes fully off, so calling the word does nothing. The host, the ball and the notification stay, and tapping the ball still listens for one sentence. This is a switch for right now; it does not touch the permission above
Power save is on: the microphone is closed and the wake word does nothing; tapping the ball still listens for one sentence (turn the switch below off to go back)
No schedule; tap to write one range, for example %1$s
Roughly %1$s; power save starts and ends on its own inside it
Inside that range right now (%1$s), so power save is in effect
One range, written like 23:00-07:00 (crossing midnight is fine). Clearing the line turns the schedule off
That does not read as a time range; write one like 23:00-07:00 (hours 0-23, minutes 0-59)
Identical start and end is an empty window, which would never save power; pick another time or clear the line to turn the schedule off
The wake word model is not downloaded yet; the download row below is what gets it
What a hit does beyond buzzing, beeping and bringing the app forward. The two mode rows go through the same command path as saying it out loud, and that table lives on the host side in one place
Also switch back to phone mode
A 500 ms buzz when the word is heard; off leaves the short beep, and the app still comes forward

On: a small ball stays over other apps - tap it to speak, hold it for a menu, drag it to an edge to tuck it away. It needs the display-over-other-apps permission, and a missing one is named instead of failing quietly
The ball is not on screen right now
The display-over-other-apps permission is missing, so the switch above will not put a ball up
The host has not reported a GUI address yet; the ball can talk, while the keyboard strip waits for that address

Move the ball up a little before dragging it sideways: while it hugs the left or right edge, dragging it straight inward crosses the system\'s back gesture first, which leaves the ball where it was and takes you out of the app instead
The ball did not come off, so it is still on screen: %1$s
There is no dsh GUI address yet, so the keyboard strip cannot open (try again once the host is up)
This device has no window manager, so no ball can be drawn
The system refused the floating window: %1$s
The voice inbox is not writable, so that line was not sent
The app could not be brought to the front: %1$s
Not listening to this one any more; tap again to start it
It did not stop: the foreground service did not take that command
The host is not up, so that mode command cannot go out
The host is not up yet, so this line is queued: it goes out once the host is running
The inbox is not writable, so that line was not sent
The wake word model is not downloaded yet; use that row in the settings page
A reply is being spoken, so it is not listening
The interrupt did not go out: the voice inbox is not writable
On: every finished reply is spoken out loud. Off: nothing is spoken on its own, while asking for a line (lw_speak) and the Listen row below still work
Cut off what is being said right now
On: the rate set on the system\'s text-to-speech page is what you hear. Turning this off, or dragging the slider below, makes this app set its own
Following the system setting; drag this to choose one here
This voice is simply a quiet one; dragging up adds gain
What you hear above 100%% is gain; the ceiling is 300%%
In percent, from %1$d to %2$d; 100%% is this voice\'s own level
The system engine keeps its own volume and this app has no API for it: speaking with that engine follows the phone\'s media volume. The slider shows up with an imported voice
The engine has not come up yet; tap to try again
This engine lists no Chinese voice, so only the system page can help
In use; pick a voice below
Speaks with a sherpa-onnx model from the voices directory; slower to start, but the voice is yours
Speaks through Microsoft Edge\'s read-aloud endpoint with no key; the voices are the ones it offers online
An endpoint-accepted voice name such as zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural; blank goes back to the default
Posts the text to an OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint and speaks with the voice that service gives
Fill in the address and key below
Not set yet: for example https://api.openai.com, or your own gateway
A domain, .../v1 or the full endpoint all work; /v1/audio/speech is appended when missing
Not set yet; leave it blank when your own gateway needs no key
Set (kept in this app\'s preferences only)
Sent as Bearer; kept in this app\'s preference file and never echoed back
A model name the endpoint accepts, such as tts-1; blank goes back to the default
A voice name the endpoint accepts, such as alloy; blank goes back to the default
This engine\'s loudness comes from the service and the phone\'s media volume; the gain here only applies to the imported model
Nothing found under %1$s; drop a model directory there and tap to scan again
%1$s model; tap to speak with it
%1$s\nOne directory per voice; tap to scan again
Where the engine itself, its voice packs and its own rate live; this app can only pick among the voices that engine offers
Says one line with the voice and rate above, so the choice can be judged by ear
This is how a reply will be spoken.
These permissions are switched on and off by the user, and DSH-LW is free to build on them.
Notifications the model posts with lw_notify
This runs only if you tap OK; waiting %1$d seconds
